extracted.intended_audience: trademark applicants, attorneys, and IP practitioners in Turkey; trademark Office staff
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory rules and procedural requirements for filing, prosecuting, opposing, registering, maintaining, licensing, revoking, and enforcing trademarks and related rights (collective/guarantee marks, geographical indications) under Turkish law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibition-based priority right
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural or legal entities who display goods or services at national or internationally recognized exhibitions in Turkey or in Paris Convention/WTO countries and present a certified reproduction of the trademark shall enjoy a priority right to file an identical trademark application in Turkey within six months following the display.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the goods/services were displayed before the official opening date, priority commences from the date they were put on display. If multiple applications arise from the same exhibition, the person who first displayed the goods/services benefits from priority; if displayed simultaneously, the person who filed first benefits. Applications filed later by third parties for identical or indistinguishably similar trademarks covering the priority date shall be refused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request and proof of priority right
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must state the priority right to be relied on at filing and deposit the associated fee; the priority certificate must be submitted within three months following the application date or the request is deemed not made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The effect and results of accepted priority rights are conferred as of the dates set out in the priority provisions (Article 12). Procedure and rules regarding priority requests are set by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple priority claims rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If more than one priority right is claimed for an application, priority commences from the date of the first valid priority right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural details are determined by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of international (Madrid) applications
rubrics_metrics.description: International applications filed under the Madrid Protocol are treated as if filed directly at the Turkish Office, deemed filed at the first hour and minute of the international application date; where multiple international applications share the same date, the one with the smaller international registration number is deemed filed first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A national application filed after the international application's date cannot be used to refuse the international application; later-dated national applications are re-examined taking into account the earlier international application. Fees for Madrid Protocol proceedings are determined by communiqué.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal/procedural examination and application date finalization
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office formally examines conformity with filing requirements; if no deficiencies, the application date/time is the reception date/hour/minute. If deficiencies exist, the applicant has two months to remedy them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deficiencies related to certain mandatory elements (subparagraphs a, b, c, ç of Article 11) cause the application date to be the date the deficiency is remedied. Other deficiencies (d, e, f) do not affect the application date. Failure to remedy deficiencies within the period leads to cancellation, although unpaid class fees may result in partial examination for paid classes. Failure to remedy priority-related deficiencies causes loss of the priority right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination on absolute grounds and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: If no formal deficiencies, the Office examines the application on substantive absolute grounds (e.g., Article 5). If the mark cannot be registered for some or all goods/services, it is refused for those goods/services; applications that pass are published in the Bulletin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a refusal is decided after publication, that decision is also published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party observations after publication
rubrics_metrics.description: After publication, any person may submit written, reasoned observations to the Office asserting that the published trademark should not be registered under the absolute grounds (Article 5), except for subparagraph (ç), until registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observers are not parties to Office proceedings. The Office will evaluate observations and may refuse the application partially or wholly if the observations are found correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to publication timing and formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Oppositions to a published application must be filed in writing with grounds by relevant persons within two months following publication; the opposition fee must be paid and payment information submitted within the opposition period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If grounds or fee/payment information are not submitted within the period, the opposition is deemed not to have been made (i.e., rejected on procedural grounds). Specific procedural rules are set by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of oppositions and proof of genuine use
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office requests the applicant's observations and may require additional documents; if requested materials are not provided, the opposition is examined on existing information. For oppositions based on certain relative grounds (Article 6), where the earlier mark was registered for at least five years at the relevant date, the opponent may be required to prove genuine use of the earlier mark in the five years before the later application's date or to justify non-use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the opponent fails to prove genuine use, the opposition shall be refused. If use is shown only for some goods/services, the opposition is considered only for those goods/services. The Office may encourage reconciliation; further procedural rules by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals to the Office (time limit and formalities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties adversely affected by Office decisions may appeal in writing with grounds to the Office within two months from notification; the appeal fee must be paid within the period and payment information submitted, or the appeal is deemed not made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After expiration of the appeal period, grounds may not be altered and new grounds cannot be added. Procedural compliance (timeliness and fee) is mandatory for admissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of appeals by the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals without formal deficiency are examined by the Board, which requests parties' observations and may request additional information; if materials are not submitted, the appeal is examined on existing information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may encourage reconciliation and its decision is final for the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for registration entry
rubrics_metrics.description: An application that has no deficiencies or whose deficiencies have been remedied, has been examined and published, has no unresolved oppositions (or oppositions rejected), and for which all missing documents and proof of registration fee payment are submitted within prescribed periods shall be recorded in the registry and published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to deposit the registration fee and submit payment information within the prescribed period leads to abolition. A mark recorded while stages remain incomplete is not deemed registered; re-registration may be ordered without charging the fee again under certain conditions. The registry is open to the public, and certified copies are available upon fee payment. Procedure details are by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of protection and renewal timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark protection term is ten years from the application date and renewable for ten-year periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal requests must be filed by the proprietor within six months before expiry with payment information; late renewal is allowed within six months after expiry upon payment of an additional fee. Renewal can cover only part of the goods/services. For collective trademarks, a request by any company in the group suffices. Renewal is effective the day after the previous registration expires and is recorded and published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing: types, default rules, and quality control
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademarks may be licensed for part or all registered goods/services as exclusive or non-exclusive; the default is non-exclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-exclusive licensors may themselves use the mark or grant further licenses. Exclusive licensors cannot grant third-party licenses and, unless reserved, may not themselves use the mark. Licensors may not transfer license-derived rights or grant sublicenses unless agreed. Licensors must take measures to guarantee the quality of the licensee's goods/services; licensees must comply with contract terms, failing which the proprietor may enforce trademark rights against the licensee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and standing for invalidation (court action)
rubrics_metrics.description: If conditions in Articles 5 or 6 exist (absolute/relative invalidity grounds), invalidation shall be decided by the court on request. Persons with interests, public prosecutors or relevant public institutions/organizations may bring invalidation actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invalidation is claimed against registered proprietors or their successors; the Office is not a party. If a mark registered contrary to certain grounds acquires distinctiveness through use before the invalidation request, it shall not be invalidated. Partial invalidation may be ordered for some goods/services. Altering the trademark representation as a result of invalidation is not permitted. Acquiescence in use for five successive years by a proprietor generally bars invalidation unless the later registration was in bad faith. In Art 6 invalidation proceedings, the genuine-use provisions of Article 19(2) may be asserted as a defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and procedure for revocation (Office action)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may revoke a trademark on request in specified situations: (a) existence of conditions in Article 9(1) (non-use), (b) mark becoming generic due to proprietor's actions or failure to act, (c) mark misleading the public about nature/quality/origin due to use by proprietor or with consent, (ç) use contrary to Article 32 (collective/guarantee specification rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interested persons may request revocation against the proprietor or successors. If genuine use occurs between the end of the five-year period and the revocation request date, revocation under (a) is refused. Use carried out expressly because a revocation request was anticipated (within three months before submission) is disregarded. Partial revocation may be ordered. Change of right owner during examination does not interrupt proceedings. Revocation requests are notified to proprietor who must submit evidence within one month (one-month extension permissible); the Office may demand additional information before deciding. Procedure rules are by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects and retroactivity of invalidation and revocation decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Invalidation decisions are effective from the trademark's application date and the trademark is deemed never to have had protection; revocation decisions are effective from the date the revocation request was submitted but may be backdated if conditions existed earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retroactive effect does not prejudice finalized/enforced court judgments or contracts established and performed prior to the decision, though fees paid under such contracts may be partially recovered on equitable grounds. Final invalidation/revocation decisions are effective erga omnes; the court sends finalized invalidation judgments ex officio to the Office and registries are updated and published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other causes and effects of termination (surrender, expiry, withdrawal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark rights terminate by expiry of the protection term without renewal, or by surrender by the proprietor. Termination takes effect when the cause occurs. Proprietors may surrender all or part of the registered goods/services in writing; surrender takes effect on entry in the register and is published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks cannot be surrendered without consent of recorded licensees or registered right owners, and cannot be surrendered if a third party claims rights and an interlocutory injunction is recorded. Applications may be withdrawn before registration, and surrender-withdrawal provisions apply similarly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts constituting trademark infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Infringement includes: (a) use of the trademark as defined (Article 7) without proprietor consent; (b) counterfeiting by using the trademark or a confusingly similar mark without consent; (c) while aware (or should be aware) of counterfeit, selling, distributing, putting on market, offering, importing, exporting, possessing for commercial purposes products bearing the infringed trademark; (ç) broadening or transferring rights given by license to third parties without consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defenses available under Article 19(2) (genuine use considerations) may be asserted in infringement proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal sanctions for trademark infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Criminal penalties apply for commercial acts infringing trademarks: producing/providing services/marketing/selling/importing/exporting/buying/possessing/transporting/storing infringing goods is punishable by 1–3 years imprisonment and judicial fine up to 20,000 days; removal of a protection sign from product/packaging punishable by 1–3 years or up to 5,000 days fine; unauthorized disposition of trademark rights (transfer/licensing/pledging) punishable by 2–4 years and up to 5,000 days fine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If offenses are committed by a legal entity, specific security measures may also be applied. To impose these criminal sanctions, the trademark must be registered in Turkey. Investigation and prosecution of these crimes are subject to a complaint; a seller who provides information leading to detection of producers/seizure may avoid sentencing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guarantee mark definition and use restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: A guarantee mark is a sign that guarantees common characteristics of undertakings, production methods, geographical origin and quality under the control of the proprietor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of a guarantee mark for goods/services of the proprietor or economically linked undertakings is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective mark definition and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: A collective mark is a sign used by a group of undertakings, producers, traders or service providers to distinguish their goods/services from those of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collective marks serve to distinguish the goods/services of the group from others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical specification requirement for guarantee and collective marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing an application for registration of a guarantee or collective mark must be accompanied by a technical specification indicating the procedure and rules for use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guarantee mark specifications must indicate common characteristics covered, methods of use, inspection procedures and frequencies after grant, and sanctions for contrary use. Collective mark specifications must specify undertakings authorized to use the mark, membership conditions, terms of use and any sanctions. All group undertakings must act collectively to register or surrender a collective mark, but each undertaking may bring legal proceedings individually. Amendments to specifications are not applicable until Office approval. If specifications lack required content or contravene public order/morality, the owner is notified to amend within six months; failure leads to rejection. Relevant persons may request revocation if the owner fails to prevent continued contrary use. Procedure rules are by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of products eligible for geographical indication (GI) or traditional speciality guaranteed (TSG)
rubrics_metrics.description: Food, agricultural, mining, handicraft and industrial products that result from the interaction of natural and human factors and comply with the statutory provisions are eligible for geographical indication or traditional speciality guaranteed protection upon registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration is required to obtain protection under these provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellation of origin, designation of origin, and TSG criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographical indication is a sign indicating a product associated with a locality, area, region or country by an apparent characteristic, reputation or other features. Appellation of origin identifies products from a designated geographical area whose all or principal characteristics derive exclusively from natural or human factors attributable to that area where production, processing and other operations take place. Designation of origin identifies products associated with a region due to characteristic or reputation where at least one production/processing step takes place within the designated area. Names traditionally used in daily language without a geographic name may also qualify. Traditional Speciality Guaranteed applies to names traditionally used for at least thirty years to describe products that originate from traditional production/processing methods or traditional composition, or meet other listed conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification (appellation vs designation) depends on whether all/principal characteristics derive exclusively from the geographical area (appellation) or at least one step takes place there (designation). TSG focuses on traditional character rather than geographic link; the statute lists specific qualifying conditions (e.g., traditional method or composition).
